_comment: CAPABILITY suite for the Db2 CDC stream source with initial_load UNDER LIVE CHANGES, over every table of the employees model and its xp_sentinel (functions/caps_db2cdc_initial_load.py::db2cdc_initial_load_live). The same stages as postgrescdc_initial_load_live: (1) domains -- create the db2cdc domain, install the employees model, load the m seed (10k employees), its operations appended to ${XP_WORK_DIR}/ops.jsonl (--emit-ops) -- as every data command below appends its own; (2) live -- `sentinel-data --key after-create-data`, then start `churn` in the background: 20 passes a second apart, `modify-data --ops Mix --sets 192` -- ~1000 CDC rows each: 64 inserts, 64 updates, 64 deletes (a deleted employee cascades to dept_emp, dept_manager, titles and salaries); it keeps running through the stages below; (3) collections; (4) functions -- register the @stream_publisher, which STARTS it: its snapshot is taken over tables changing under it, and every change after it arrives as a CDC row, over the domain's own CD tables (${D0__CD_TABLE_PREFIX}<TABLE>, registered with the model), from the commit sequence the snapshot's brief table lock pinned; asncap stages each change a moment after it commits; (5) live -- wait for churn to finish, then `sentinel-data --key after-churn`; (6) sentinel -- hold until both keys are in xp_sentinel_changes (at most 5m each); (7) execute -- scripts/verify_cdc_ops.py checks every <table>_changes against ops.jsonl, the snapshot as the state the operations before it leave and the changes after it one by one; (8) monitor. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite container-connectors/db2cdc_initial_load_live --keep`. verify-ops runs with --cascades logged --noops logged, what the Db2 log is expected to carry -- unconfirmed until the stream starts (DB2_25, see caps_db2cdc_initial_load.py).
